title: The festival leaving Edinburgh
gist: On its 50th anniversary the Edinburgh TV Festival will relocate to Manchester from 2027 after a bidding process citing accessibility, affordability and sustainability; the piece argues the move severs the event from the Edinburgh Fringe ecosystem that fuelled its success and leaves the UK TV industry weaker and more fragmented.

insights.claim: The Edinburgh TV Festival will leave Edinburgh after 50 years and move to Manchester from 2027, which won a bidding process the organisers said was driven by challenges around accessibility, affordability and sustainability.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: A structural shift in where the UK TV industry’s dealmaking and talent-spotting will physically concentrate.
insights.quote: amid increasing challenges around accessibility, affordability and sustainability
insights.locator: and yet this will be the last time

insights.claim: Founder Lynda Myles argues Edinburgh provides a unique life source for the TV Festival that cannot be reproduced elsewhere, and that the city and the festival are indelibly linked for the international TV community.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Frames location as intangible brand capital that a relocation risks destroying.
insights.locator: In a letter to the festival’s current organisers

insights.claim: Proximity to the Edinburgh Fringe, the world’s biggest arts festival, was long seen as key to the TV Festival’s success and helped executives discover hits including Fleabag and Baby Reindeer.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Identifies the talent-discovery pipeline the industry loses by moving away from the Fringe.
insights.locator: Proximity to the world’s biggest arts festival

insights.claim: Isabel Hilton argues that by exiting Edinburgh the TV Festival leaves behind a weaker, more fragmented UK TV industry.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: The core downside claim: the move imposes a diffuse cost on the whole sector beyond the host city.
insights.quote: by exiting Edinburgh the TV Festival leaves behind a weaker, more fragmented industry
insights.locator: But the outcome remains the same

insights.claim: The festival was founded in 1976 by Lynda Myles and Gus MacDonald out of the Edinburgh International Film Festival, after Myles noticed leading British directors like Stephen Frears, Ken Loach and Mike Leigh were not working exclusively in cinema.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Origin context establishing the event’s original avant-garde purpose against which its current drift is measured.
insights.locator: It was against this backdrop of new ideas

insights.claim: Hilton argues the relocation shows the festival—independent since 2001—has lost sight of what it was for and why it was held in Edinburgh for five decades.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Reads the move as a symptom of mission drift rather than a neutral logistics choice.

insights.claim: The James MacTaggart Memorial Lecture has drifted from its radical founding spirit—no fewer than three Murdochs (Rupert 1989, James 2009, Elisabeth 2012) have delivered it—while recent speakers like Dorothy Byrne and Michaela Coel are closer to the original brief.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: The lecture’s speaker roster tracks the commercialisation of the industry it represents.

insights.claim: This year’s keynote MacTaggart Lecture was delivered by YouTube executive Pedro Pina.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: A platform executive headlining signals where power in the TV value chain now sits.
insights.locator: with most public attention likely drawn

insights.claim: The revelation that the TV Festival had received some £600,000 of public funding over the years intensified Scottish anger at the move, prompting Screen Scotland to explore a replacement festival for Edinburgh.
insights.speaker: Isabel Hilton
insights.so_what: Public subsidy makes the relocation a political and accountability issue, not just a private organisational one.
insights.locator: For Scottish players, the move was all the more upsetting
